question.text: What will the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index be for November 26, 2026 (water-year-to-date, inches)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the water-year-to-date value of the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index (CDEC station code 8SI) for the observation date 2026-11-26 — i.e. the value in the cumulative 'RAIN' column (inches) on the row dated 11/26/2026 in the daily data table at https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/QueryDaily?end=2026-11-26&s=8SI (for example, a row showing RAIN = 5.83 resolves as 5.83). The first value CDEC publishes for that date is used, and later revisions of CDEC's provisional data do not change the resolution. If no value for 11/26/2026 has been published when resolution is attempted on November 27, 2026, resolution waits until CDEC publishes it; if CDEC never publishes a value for that date, the question is annulled. If the CDEC page is inaccessible, the value may be taken from CDEC's daily precipitation report at http://cdec.water.ca.gov/reportapp/javareports?name=DailyPrecip (the 8SI value carrying data date 11/26/2026) or otherwise from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: CDEC's date label for each daily precipitation value is used as-is, regardless of the exact hourly cut-off or timezone convention behind that label; precipitation recorded after that observation does not affect the answer. The index is a DWR composite and is not recomputed from the eight individual station records by the resolver. Because CDEC re-renders its pages with current data, resolvers should preserve a copy of the page used (e.g. a Wayback Machine capture) at the time of resolution.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

Recent rows: 11/12 0.71; 11/13 +0.01 = 0.72; 11/14 +1.43 = 2.15; 11/15 +0.07 = 2.22; 11/16 +1.22 = 3.44. Today is 11/16, so that row is probably a partial day and may still change. Earlier rows: 10/22 0.22, 10/23 0.46, 11/01 0.55, 11/04 0.71. [CDEC 8SI](https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/QueryDaily?end=2026-11-16&s=8SI)

## 2. Current status

- Nothing settles the question yet. About 2.7 in has fallen since 11/13, more than the whole water year before that. To finish at a given value, the index needs that value minus 3.44 in between now and the 11/26 row.
- 2026-11-16: NWS Sacramento expects a further 1.00-1.50 in for the Sierra today, mostly in the morning, with dry weather by midnight. Some of this may already be in the 3.44 figure. [NWS STO AFD](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=STO&issuedby=STO&product=AFD)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-16: NWS Sacramento forecast discussion:
  - A strong storm runs from Tuesday night (11/17) to early Friday (11/20), bringing **2 to 3.5 in liquid over the mountains**, 1.5-2.75 in in the foothills and 1.25-2 in in the Valley.
  - The latest trend raised totals from I-80 south and "slightly decrease[d] amounts over the northern mountains." Most 8SI gauges (Mt Shasta, Shasta Dam, Mineral, Quincy, Brush Creek) are in that northern zone.
  - Snow levels are 3,500-6,000 ft, with 1-2 ft of snow above 5,000 ft.
  - The office sees "increasing confidence towards the active pattern returning for the weekend," possibly continuing "into Thanksgiving week."
  - [NWS STO AFD](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=STO&issuedby=STO&product=AFD)
- 2026-11-16: The Watchers reports two atmospheric rivers, with the stronger one arriving late on 11/17. It gives no liquid totals for the northern Sierra. [Watchers](https://watchers.news/2026/11/16/2-atmospheric-rivers-to-bring-heavy-sierra-snow-and-california-flood-risk/)
- 2026-11-16: Winter storm watches are out with up to 48 in of snow above 8,000 ft. [AOL](https://www.aol.com/articles/winter-storm-watches-issued-48-085652000.html)
- 2026-11-15: KCRA calls the midweek storm possibly the strongest of the season: 1-2 in Valley, 2-3 in foothills, up to 3 ft of snow at the peaks. [KCRA](https://www.kcra.com/article/northern-california-evening-forecast-nov-15-2026-1794832352/74439116)
- 2026-11-15: First significant Sierra snowfall of the season. [CBS SF](https://www.cbsnews.com/sanfrancisco/news/first-significant-snowfall-sierra-optimism/)
- 2026-11-14: The NWS cancelled the Sierra winter storm warning six hours early. [Nevada Appeal](https://www.nevadaappeal.com/news/2026/nov/14/road-controls-in-effect-over-kingsbury-grade/)

- Over this 10-day window the gain ranged from 0 to 11.3 in, with a median of about 1.9 in. The spread is very wide and driven by single storms.
- This year's 3.44 in on 11/16 is above 2023 (1.97) and 2024 (2.79), but below 2022, 2025 and 2021.
- Typical accumulation by mid-November is about 5 in (from the question background).

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no market or expert forecast on the 8SI itself.
- Related Kalshi prices as of 2026-11-16 (all from the collected price list):
  - San Francisco November rain: above 6 in 0.70, above 7 in 0.42, above 8 in 0.31. That implies a wet rest of the month.
  - Los Angeles November rain: above 2 in 0.85, above 3 in 0.34.
  - Sierra-at-Tahoe opening before Dec 13: 0.62.
- Polymarket "California winter 2026-27 wetter or drier?": 0.525 for "wetter".

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution and official outlooks

- 11/17 (Tue, daytime): A dry break with frost possible. [NWS STO](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=STO&issuedby=STO&product=AFD)
- 11/17 night to 11/20 morning: Main storm, 2-3.5 in liquid in the mountains, slightly lower trend for the northern mountains. Thunderstorms are possible 11/18-11/19.
- 11/21-11/22 weekend and Thanksgiving week (Thanksgiving is 11/26): The NWS says the active pattern is likely to return.
- 2026-11-15 CPC outlooks: [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/610day/fxus06.html)
  - 6-10 day (11/21-11/25): above-normal precipitation favoured along the West Coast, over 60% chance for parts of coastal central and northern California.
  - 8-14 day (11/23-11/29): over 50% chance from the Pacific Northwest to northern and central California. A slow-moving deep trough sits offshore, but CPC notes uncertainty about how close it comes to the coast.
- I did not get WPC 7-day QPF numbers for the specific 8SI stations.
- Data caveat: the resolver uses the first value CDEC publishes for 11/26. Quick checks around 11/27 could catch a partial-day figure, and estimated ("e") flags appear in past years' data.

## Northern Sierra 8-Station Index (8SI) for Nov 26, 2026: research notes

**Bottom line:** The index already stands at 3.44 in. CNRFC's forecast adds roughly 3.4 to 4.3 in through about Nov 22, and outlooks favour more storms through Nov 29. The range of 1.0 to 16.0 in has a firm floor at 3.44, because the index is cumulative and can't fall.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The CDEC 8SI daily table shows these rows. [CDEC](https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/QueryDaily?end=2026-11-16&s=8SI)

| 11/13 | 0.01 | 0.72 |
| 11/14 | 1.43 | 2.15 |
| 11/15 | 0.07 | 2.22 |
| 11/16 | 1.22 | **3.44** (latest) |

- Earlier context: 0.47 in on 10/31 and 0.71 in on 11/04, then no rain Nov 5-12.
- The 11/16 row may cover only part of the day and could still be revised; I couldn't confirm CDEC's cut-off time. All values are marked provisional.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value is 3.44 in and cannot go below that.

  - Sacramento at Delta: about 3.8 in
  - Feather at Oroville: about 3.4 in
  - Yuba at Englebright: about 3.3 in

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

[The Watchers](https://watchers.news/2026/11/16/2-atmospheric-rivers-to-bring-heavy-sierra-snow-and-california-flood-risk/)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on the 8SI itself.
- Related Kalshi markets (prices from 2026-11-16):

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 to 11 days. The 11/26 row should appear on CDEC around November 27, 2026.

(b) The CDEC 8SI water-year-to-date value is 3.44 in on 11/16/2026. This is probably a partial day, after +1.43 on 11/14 and +1.22 so far on 11/16.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 3.4 to 3.7 in, depending on how much of today's forecast 1 to 1.5 in is still to post.

(d) If the current trend continued, the outcome would be roughly 8 to 9 in:
- About 3.6 by the end of today.
- About 2 to 3 in from the main 11/17-11/20 storm. NWS gives 2 to 3.5 in for the mountains, trending a bit lower over the northern Sierra.
- About 1.5 to 3 in from the active pattern returning over the weekend and Thanksgiving week.

(e) Historical variation: across the last five years, the change from 11/16 to 11/26 ranged from 0 to +11.3 in, with a median of about 1.9 in. Big jumps come from single atmospheric rivers. This year, about 2 to 3 in for the first storm is already close to certain.

(f) Experts and markets point wet:
- NWS forecasts 2 to 3.5 in for the mountains midweek, with an active pattern likely continuing.
- CPC favours above-normal precipitation for both the 6-10 day and 8-14 day windows.
- Kalshi prices San Francisco November rain above 6 in at 0.70 and above 8 in at 0.31, which implies a very wet rest of the month.
- There is no direct market on the 8SI.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: the midweek storm underperforms in the north, at about 1.2 in averaged across the stations. The weekend and Thanksgiving-week trough then stays offshore or goes south, and the 11/26 figure is published low or partial. The result would be about 4.5 to 5 in.
- High: the offshore trough moves in and drives a strong atmospheric river into the northern Sierra over 11/22-11/25, like 2024's +9.7 in over three days. Together with the midweek storm, that could push the index to 15 to 18 in.

(b) The latest value is 3.44 in on 11/16/2026, per CDEC 8SI. That row is likely a partial day, since NWS expected 1.00-1.50 in for the Sierra today, mostly in the morning.

(c) If nothing changed, the index would end at about 3.4 to 3.7 in. The higher end allows for the rest of today's rain.

(d) If the current trend continued, the total would be around 8 to 9 in:
- The 11/17-11/20 storm is forecast at 2-3.5 in liquid in the mountains. Amounts trend slightly lower for the northern zone, so I expect roughly 2-3 in on the index.
